code_status: deployable constructed code; population reach unmeasured
communities_potentially_served: Literate speakers of named Slavic languages who can read the supplied Latin or Cyrillic arm and whose comprehension is demonstrated at the required endpoint
communities_explicitly_not_served: The Slavic-family population as a whole; non-Slavic minorities; readers who cannot use the supplied script; any named Slavic community not separately evidenced
scripts_or_modalities: ordinary Slavic Latin; Cyrillic; extended etymological orthography only as optional research display
zero_study_evidence: A proponent-authored, self-selected online cloze task had 1,766 respondents; mean six of seven deleted words recovered (84% rescaled), with 18% below five of seven. This is word recovery, not proposition or learning transfer.
learned_or_exposure_evidence: Bulgarian follow-up found script and case difficulties; 50.8% recognized the relevant noun-case endings and performance varied by age/education. No fixed orientation-time or mathematical transfer estimate exists.
shared_source_parallel_standard_reuse: Can reuse one semantic source for Latin/Cyrillic supplements, abstracts, glossaries and aligned comparison material; natural-language outputs remain separately labelled.
script_conversion_role: Latin↔Cyrillic conversion is an additional delivery/QA arm, not new comprehension evidence; typography, proper nouns and morphology still need audit.
speculative_construction: No: a stable code exists, but any claim of family-wide functional reach is speculative.
math_worked_examples_modifier: Possible positive only for symbol-dense examples and already-skilled readers; not directly tested.
math_definition_theorem_modifier: No automatic credit: quantifier, negation, hypothesis and necessity/sufficiency wording must be recovered.
math_proof_modifier: No automatic credit: case, aspect, referents and discourse links carry proof logic.
math_word_problem_modifier: No automatic credit; linguistic complexity remains part of the task.
unique_gain_rule: Count only community×script×endpoint strata with evidence of usable comprehension beyond their strongest existing edition or academic lingua franca.
double_count_rule: Assign each beneficiary once by full capability profile; subtract overlap with natural Slavic editions, Russian/English proficiency and both script arms.
uncertainty_and_evidence_gap: Self-selection, cloze ceiling, education effects, no representative sampling, no technical-prose transfer and no population denominator.
current_evidence_disposition: Pilot/supplement; unranked as a family-wide language target until community-specific functional bounds exist.

bridge_name: Pan-Turkic constructed language / Common Turkic Alphabet
bridge_class: speculative constructed zonal bridge plus orthography proposal
code_status: no common language specification with functional evidence; 34-letter alphabet is a proposed orthography
communities_potentially_served: No population may currently be assigned; possible future close-pair experiments must name Oghuz, Kipchak, Karluk, Siberian/Northeastern or Oghur communities separately
communities_explicitly_not_served: The Turkic-family population as a whole; speakers outside a tested close pair; users of Cyrillic or Perso-Arabic scripts not literate in the proposed Latin arm
scripts_or_modalities: proposed 34-letter Latin alphabet; existing national Latin, Cyrillic and Perso-Arabic scripts remain separate arms
zero_study_evidence: No controlled comprehension study of a deployable common Turkic code was located. The alphabet commission reports an orthographic proposal, not a common language or comprehension result.
learned_or_exposure_evidence: Natural Turkish→Azerbaijani evidence is narrow, one-directional and based on 30 Turkish participants; it cannot be generalized to all Turkic branches.
shared_source_parallel_standard_reuse: Reusable infrastructure is limited to terminology concordances, cognate/false-friend maps and script-aware search; it does not justify one textbook code.
script_conversion_role: The proposed alphabet may support mapping among Latin standards; it does not confer Latin literacy or convert Cyrillic/Perso-Arabic audiences into readers.
speculative_construction: Yes: both family-wide language reach and a unified technical register are speculative.
math_worked_examples_modifier: Unknown; shared morphology and formulas do not establish shared technical vocabulary.
math_definition_theorem_modifier: No credit; branch-specific syntax and lexicon control theorem meaning.
math_proof_modifier: No credit; agglutinative forms, evidentiality and reference chains vary.
math_word_problem_modifier: No credit; ordinary vocabulary remains branch- and community-specific.
unique_gain_rule: Zero until a named community, script and endpoint are independently tested.
double_count_rule: Never use the Turkic-family total; pair-level unions only, with exposure and bilingualism overlap removed.
uncertainty_and_evidence_gap: No common code, no proposition test, no training burden, multiple scripts and substantial branch divergence.
current_evidence_disposition: Research infrastructure only; not a scored bridge-language edition.

code_status: two established natural standards; directional comprehension evidence
communities_potentially_served: Turkish readers of Azerbaijani and Azerbaijani readers of Turkish must be modelled separately; national Latin standards only unless another script is tested
communities_explicitly_not_served: Other Oghuz communities; all non-Oghuz Turkic communities; Iranian Azerbaijani readers not literate in the tested script; any untested direction
scripts_or_modalities: Turkish Latin; Azerbaijani Latin; Iranian Azerbaijani Perso-Arabic only as a separate unevidenced arm
zero_study_evidence: A 30-person study tested Turkish participants' written and spoken Azerbaijani and found intelligibility lower than participants expected; the study does not establish the reverse direction or technical comprehension.
learned_or_exposure_evidence: Exposure and orientation can affect understanding, but fixed hours and mathematical transfer are unmeasured.
shared_source_parallel_standard_reuse: High potential for a common semantic source with separately labelled Turkish and Azerbaijani lexical layers, false-friend alerts and parallel abstracts.
script_conversion_role: Latin-to-Perso-Arabic conversion changes the eligible population and requires a separate lexical/orthographic target; it is not a mechanical substitute.
speculative_construction: No for the two natural standards; yes for extrapolation beyond the tested direction/pair.
math_worked_examples_modifier: Possible for formula-dense examples after terminology mapping; no direct test.
math_definition_theorem_modifier: Low confidence without explicit technical-term mapping.
math_proof_modifier: No direct evidence; directional miscues can be logically consequential.
math_word_problem_modifier: No direct evidence; false friends can cause confident errors.
unique_gain_rule: Count only directional, script-literate readers who gain access beyond their existing Turkish/Azerbaijani and other strong-language routes.
double_count_rule: Separate TR→AZ and AZ→TR; subtract bilingual/exposure overlap; never expand to a Turkic-family union.
uncertainty_and_evidence_gap: Small one-directional study; technical register and second script absent.
current_evidence_disposition: Pair-specific parallel aid/pilot, not a pan-Turkic edition.

bridge_class: learned receptive strategy across natural standards
code_status: established pedagogical approach; not one constructed code
communities_potentially_served: Readers of exact Romance standards who receive a defined intercomprehension module and are tested on specified target standards; own-language production can be retained
communities_explicitly_not_served: Untested Romance varieties; Romance creoles; low-literacy readers; readers for whom French/Romanian or another target remains below endpoint; family population without training
scripts_or_modalities: national Latin orthographies; Romanian diacritics; accessibility variants separately scoped
zero_study_evidence: In a 16-language European study, Romance spoken cloze averaged about 36.7% with large pair/direction differences; Italian/Portuguese listeners understood Spanish better than reverse; French and Romanian were poor bridge targets for many pairs.
learned_or_exposure_evidence: A 21-hour module with Italian children aged 10–11 (n=19 within-subject comprehension questionnaire; smaller intervention/control groups for EFL) produced initial plurilingual reading competence; authors call for further confirmation. No mathematical endpoint.
shared_source_parallel_standard_reuse: Strong as a common semantic source plus natural editions, cognate/false-friend cues and a taught receptive layer; weak as a single median register.
script_conversion_role: Same Latin base does not erase orthographic and diacritic differences; conversion is not the main barrier.
speculative_construction: No for pedagogy; yes for claiming one pan-Romance code or blanket zero-study access.
math_worked_examples_modifier: Potential positive in symbol-dense material after short orientation; untested.
math_definition_theorem_modifier: No automatic credit; familiar Latinate forms can produce false confidence.
math_proof_modifier: No automatic credit; proof discourse and scope remain language-specific.
math_word_problem_modifier: No automatic credit; word-problem language is an independent difficulty source.
unique_gain_rule: Count only post-module learners who cross a preregistered functional endpoint for a named target standard and lack equivalent existing access.
double_count_rule: One learner is assigned once across native Romance, learned Romance, English/French and intercomprehension capability; use pair-direction evidence, not family totals.
uncertainty_and_evidence_gap: Small training study; spoken cloze is not reading transfer; technical-math transfer and durability unmeasured.
current_evidence_disposition: Taught access layer attached to natural editions; population effect remains partially identified.

code_status: established natural standards; directional evidence
communities_potentially_served: Portuguese readers of Spanish and Italian readers of Spanish are the strongest directions in the reviewed European cloze evidence; reverse directions are separate strata
communities_explicitly_not_served: French/Romanian readers by inference; Romance creoles; speakers of other standards; readers lacking script literacy or sufficient literacy
scripts_or_modalities: national Latin orthographies
zero_study_evidence: European spoken cloze showed Portuguese listeners 77.4% on Spanish and Italian listeners 65.7% on Spanish; reverse directions were weaker. These are spoken cloze results among young educated participants, not educational transfer.
learned_or_exposure_evidence: Exposure influences some results; no standardized training-hours or mathematical comprehension results.
shared_source_parallel_standard_reuse: A Spanish edition may provide a supplementary receptive route for some Portuguese/Italian readers, while lexical variants and terminology overlays can share source structure.
script_conversion_role: Orthographic proximity helps but does not establish technical comprehension.
speculative_construction: No for natural pairs; any family-wide extension is speculative.
math_worked_examples_modifier: Possible positive for symbol-dense examples, especially in the stronger direction; untested.
math_definition_theorem_modifier: No automatic credit; technical terms, negatives and relational phrases require testing.
math_proof_modifier: No direct evidence.
math_word_problem_modifier: No direct evidence; ordinary language and confidence calibration are risks.
unique_gain_rule: Only directional readers whose endpoint access improves beyond Portuguese/Italian/English/French routes.
double_count_rule: Do not sum directions or national speaker counts; remove exposure and existing Spanish proficiency; never treat one Spanish edition as pan-Romance coverage.
uncertainty_and_evidence_gap: Young educated European sample; spoken cloze; no Latin American/African/Asian variety coverage or math transfer.
current_evidence_disposition: Natural-pair overlap layer; not a constructed interlanguage.

bridge_class: constructed international auxiliary language with Romance-heavy vocabulary
code_status: stable learned code; zero-study reach not independently quantified
communities_potentially_served: Actual learned Interlingua users; zero-study Romance readers only if a named community and endpoint are independently tested
communities_explicitly_not_served: The Romance-family or global population; communities whose languages are not represented by the control-language vocabulary; readers inferred from cognate appearance
scripts_or_modalities: Latin script
zero_study_evidence: The official organization claims immediate comprehension, but the bounded search found no independent representative zero-study proposition or technical-learning test. Design vocabulary draws from Italian, Spanish/Portuguese, French, English and other European controls.
learned_or_exposure_evidence: Learning materials exist, but no source-bounded technical proficiency population or fixed acquisition burden was established here.
shared_source_parallel_standard_reuse: Could be an additional aligned abstract/control against natural Romance editions; it is not evidence for replacing them.
script_conversion_role: Not primarily a script-conversion intervention.
speculative_construction: No for the stable code; yes for untrained population reach.
math_worked_examples_modifier: Unknown; scientific cognates may help skilled readers, but this is a design expectation.
math_definition_theorem_modifier: No credit without proposition-level test.
math_proof_modifier: No credit without proof-transfer test.
math_word_problem_modifier: No credit; ordinary-word and word-problem coverage may be weaker than scientific lexicon.
unique_gain_rule: Count actual learned users or independently tested community×endpoint strata only.
double_count_rule: Subtract learned Romance/English/Latin and natural-edition access; no family multiplier.
uncertainty_and_evidence_gap: No independent representative comprehension study, no technical endpoint, unknown learned population denominator.
current_evidence_disposition: Learned-community target or research control; unranked for zero-study bridge reach.

code_status: documented design; functional reach unmeasured
communities_potentially_served: Actual learners/users and any exact Romance community later passing independent tests
communities_explicitly_not_served: All Romance speakers by default; Romanian, minoritized Romance standards and Romance creoles absent separate evidence
scripts_or_modalities: project Latin orthography with diacritics
zero_study_evidence: No independent controlled zero-study functional or mathematical comprehension study was located; present evidence is a design specification and community activity.
learned_or_exposure_evidence: Training burden and functional learned population are not established.
shared_source_parallel_standard_reuse: Could be compared as one aligned abstract/control; natural standard layers remain necessary.
script_conversion_role: Not chiefly script conversion; diacritics can create an extra rendering/literacy arm.
speculative_construction: Yes for population reach; the code itself exists as a design.
math_worked_examples_modifier: Unknown; resemblance to several Romance standards may aid gist and confidence at the same time.
math_definition_theorem_modifier: No credit; a median form may privilege Spanish/Italian-like patterns.
math_proof_modifier: No credit.
math_word_problem_modifier: No credit; ordinary lexicon and culturally situated problems untested.
unique_gain_rule: Count actual learned users or exact independently tested strata only.
double_count_rule: No family total; subtract natural Romance, English/French/Spanish/Portuguese and Interlingua overlap.
uncertainty_and_evidence_gap: No independent functional testing, no population denominator, no technical terminology validation.
current_evidence_disposition: Research control/pilot only.

code_status: draft specification; no stable evidence-backed common code
communities_potentially_served: No population may currently be assigned; a future test would require separate West/North Germanic, script and exposure strata
communities_explicitly_not_served: The Germanic-family population; English speakers; Low German, Plautdietsch, Pennsylvania Dutch, Hutterisch, Frisian, Afrikaans, Yiddish, Scots, Faroese and Nordic communities without exact evidence
scripts_or_modalities: draft Latin orthography; Hebrew-script Yiddish and other community orthographies are not covered
zero_study_evidence: Folksprak's own document says it is a draft and states intelligibility as a goal. Independent cloze work on natural Germanic languages shows strong pair variation: minimal-exposure English listeners averaged 8.9% across four other tested Germanic languages.
learned_or_exposure_evidence: Natural Scandinavian, Dutch–German border and Dutch–Afrikaans evidence supports narrow pairs, not a whole-family learned register.
shared_source_parallel_standard_reuse: Better pursued as natural-pair glossaries and parallel standards; one artificial edition cannot be credited with family coverage.
script_conversion_role: A Latin-only code structurally excludes Hebrew-script Yiddish readers and does not solve orthographic/community differences.
speculative_construction: Yes: both stable specification and family-wide comprehension are speculative.
math_worked_examples_modifier: Unknown; international scientific vocabulary may disproportionately reflect English/Latinate education, not Germanic commonality.
math_definition_theorem_modifier: No credit.
math_proof_modifier: No credit.
math_word_problem_modifier: No credit.
unique_gain_rule: Zero until an exact community, script and endpoint is independently tested.
double_count_rule: No Germanic-family total; subtract pervasive English/German proficiency and natural-pair access.
uncertainty_and_evidence_gap: Draft code, no functional study, severe English overlap, branch and script heterogeneity.
current_evidence_disposition: Do not treat as current educational bridge; test separate natural-pair profiles instead.

code_status: established bounded practice among Danish, Norwegian and Swedish standards
communities_potentially_served: Danish, Norwegian Bokmål/Nynorsk and Swedish readers with actual neighboring-language comprehension; written and spoken endpoints separate
communities_explicitly_not_served: Icelandic, Faroese, Finnish, Sámi, Greenlandic and other Nordic communities; anyone without sufficient neighboring-language competence
scripts_or_modalities: national Latin orthographies; Bokmål and Nynorsk remain distinct labels

learned_or_exposure_evidence: Schooling/media familiarization supplies acquired comprehension; no single fixed training burden or mathematical endpoint is available.
shared_source_parallel_standard_reuse: High: one semantic source can generate labelled Danish, Norwegian and Swedish term layers; no constructed median code is needed.
script_conversion_role: Not a script problem, but orthographic and terminology differences remain QA arms.
speculative_construction: No.
math_worked_examples_modifier: Possible positive for written symbol-dense examples; not directly tested.
math_definition_theorem_modifier: No automatic credit; national terminology and conditional language remain relevant.
math_proof_modifier: No direct evidence.
math_word_problem_modifier: No direct evidence.
unique_gain_rule: Count only readers who cross the endpoint in a neighboring edition and lack equivalent own-standard/English access.
double_count_rule: Pair and direction specific; subtract own-language editions, English proficiency and prior neighboring-language exposure.
uncertainty_and_evidence_gap: Studies center young educated Europeans and often speech; Norwegian was not in the 16-language cloze table cited here.
current_evidence_disposition: Established overlap/parallel-source layer; not a new interlanguage.

code_status: established natural standards with strong but exposure-confounded evidence
communities_potentially_served: Czech readers of Slovak and Slovak readers of Czech; each direction separately; Czech/Slovak Latin literacy assumed
communities_explicitly_not_served: Other West, East or South Slavic communities; Czech/Slovak diaspora readers without proficiency; all Slavs by extrapolation
scripts_or_modalities: Czech and Slovak Latin orthographies

learned_or_exposure_evidence: Historical media/contact exposure is a major component; no technical-math endpoint or orientation-time estimate.
shared_source_parallel_standard_reuse: Very high shared-source potential with labelled terminology/orthography and formula identity; two standards remain visible.
script_conversion_role: Not a script-conversion case.
speculative_construction: No.

math_definition_theorem_modifier: No automatic credit; technical terminology still requires direction-specific validation.
math_proof_modifier: No direct evidence.
math_word_problem_modifier: No direct evidence.
unique_gain_rule: Count directional readers newly reaching the endpoint beyond own-language and other strong-language access.
double_count_rule: Do not sum Czech and Slovak populations; one full capability profile per reader; remove cross-border/media exposure when estimating inherited access.
uncertainty_and_evidence_gap: Exposure prevents clean zero-study estimate; spoken cloze, not educational transfer.
current_evidence_disposition: Strong natural-pair overlap and shared-source case.

code_status: established natural standards; asymmetric written evidence
communities_potentially_served: Dutch readers of Afrikaans and Afrikaans readers of Dutch, separately; literate standard users
communities_explicitly_not_served: Other West Germanic communities; Low German, Frisian, Yiddish and English speakers by inference; spoken reach without testing
scripts_or_modalities: Dutch and Afrikaans Latin orthographies
zero_study_evidence: A newspaper-article cloze study found written comprehension in both directions and an asymmetry: Dutch participants understood Afrikaans more easily than South African participants understood Dutch.
learned_or_exposure_evidence: No fixed training burden or mathematical transfer estimate; English exposure may contribute and must be modelled.
shared_source_parallel_standard_reuse: High potential for aligned terminology/false-friend support, but a Dutch edition cannot be treated as an Afrikaans edition or vice versa.
script_conversion_role: Not primarily script conversion.
speculative_construction: No.
math_worked_examples_modifier: Possible positive for written examples; no math-specific test.
math_definition_theorem_modifier: No automatic credit; false friends and technical terms remain.
math_proof_modifier: No direct evidence.
math_word_problem_modifier: No direct evidence.
unique_gain_rule: Count only directional readers whose functional access crosses the endpoint beyond own-language and English routes.
double_count_rule: Separate directions; subtract English and second-language overlap; never extend to Germanic family totals.
uncertainty_and_evidence_gap: Newspaper cloze rather than education; sample/domain and English exposure limit generalization.
current_evidence_disposition: Evidence-backed natural-pair aid.

code_status: established national standards with high mutual intelligibility; cross-standard technical reach unmeasured
communities_potentially_served: Bahasa Indonesia; Malaysian Standard Malay; Brunei Standard Malay; Singapore Standard Malay, each as a labelled output; Jawi-literate strata only when a Jawi arm is supplied
communities_explicitly_not_served: Other Malayic languages and local Malay varieties; hundreds of Indonesian regional languages; colloquial Brunei Malay; readers lacking learned standard proficiency
scripts_or_modalities: Rumi/Latin national standards; Jawi as separate Malaysian/Bruneian/community arm

script_conversion_role: Rumi↔Jawi conversion is a separate literacy and QA arm; it cannot be assumed to serve all Malay-standard users.
speculative_construction: No for standards; yes for a fictitious single 'Pan-Malay' register or blanket Malayic-family reach.
math_worked_examples_modifier: Possible positive for formal symbol-dense material; terminology layer required.
math_definition_theorem_modifier: No automatic credit; national lexical differences can carry mathematical definitions.
math_proof_modifier: No direct evidence.
math_word_problem_modifier: No direct evidence; colloquial/local forms and false friends matter.
unique_gain_rule: Count readers of each labelled standard who gain access beyond their strongest existing language; cross-standard spillover only for independently bounded comprehension.
double_count_rule: Use complete profiles across Indonesian, Standard Malay, English and local languages; do not add national-standard populations or count the same bilingual twice.
uncertainty_and_evidence_gap: No representative technical transfer study; national L2 proficiency and Rumi/Jawi literacy distributions needed.
current_evidence_disposition: Strong shared-source parallel-standard case, not one interlanguage.

communities_explicitly_not_served: Slovenian, Macedonian, Bulgarian and other South Slavic communities; diaspora readers lacking standard literacy; anyone served only by erased/merged labels

math_word_problem_modifier: No direct evidence.

bridge_class: shared grammar with divergent formal lexicons and scripts

unique_gain_rule: Count only MSA-proficient strata newly accessing the material; younger/home-variety-only learners require separate access deltas.
double_count_rule: One learner once across home variety, MSA, English/French and other languages; never use an Arabic umbrella total as technical reach.
uncertainty_and_evidence_gap: Territory/stage proficiency distributions and technical-reading endpoints are missing; home varieties heterogeneous.
current_evidence_disposition: Established learned-standard target with stage-specific bounds, not an interlanguage multiplier.

bridge_class: learned regional lingua franca / natural language
code_status: established L1/L2 standard; technical L2 proficiency unmeasured
communities_potentially_served: Named L1 and proficient L2 Kiswahili readers in Tanzania, Kenya, Uganda, Rwanda, Burundi, eastern/central DRC and other evidenced settings
communities_explicitly_not_served: Other Bantu languages by genealogical inference; all East/Central Africans; local-language-only learners; Ajami readers without a supplied/tested arm
scripts_or_modalities: standard Latin; Ajami only for separately evidenced communities
zero_study_evidence: Institutional evidence establishes wide bridge use, not zero-study intelligibility with neighboring Bantu languages; family relationship provides no population credit.
learned_or_exposure_evidence: L2 reach is acquired through schooling, trade, media and policy, with large setting-specific variation; technical literacy is not equivalent to reported use.
shared_source_parallel_standard_reuse: High for one standard Kiswahili semantic edition plus regional glossary/level variants; it cannot replace local-language editions.
script_conversion_role: Ajami conversion is a separate community/script intervention, not automatic reach.
speculative_construction: No.
math_worked_examples_modifier: Positive only for readers already technically proficient; formal notation may reduce prose burden.
math_definition_theorem_modifier: No automatic bridge bonus; terminology familiarity is required.
math_proof_modifier: No automatic bridge bonus.
math_word_problem_modifier: No automatic bridge bonus; local context and narrative language remain.
unique_gain_rule: Count exact L1/proficient-L2 strata where the Kiswahili edition adds access beyond local language and English/French/Arabic routes.
double_count_rule: Territory-specific union; separate L1/L2/academic proficiency; do not use a headline global speaker/user count as technical reach.
uncertainty_and_evidence_gap: Technical-reading proficiency, stage distribution, regional terminology and accessibility evidence are incomplete.
current_evidence_disposition: Established learned natural-language bridge with territory-specific bounds.

bridge_class: existing learned academic lingua franca / overlap control
code_status: established natural language; changing learned reach
communities_potentially_served: Russian-proficient readers in each named country, cohort, stage and subject where current evidence supports technical use
communities_explicitly_not_served: National-language-only and younger cohorts without sufficient Russian; all residents of Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Uzbekistan or Turkmenistan; non-Russian minorities by default
scripts_or_modalities: Cyrillic; national-language Latin/Cyrillic/Perso-Arabic scripts remain separate
zero_study_evidence: Higher-education literature documents continuing Russian use; this is evidence of acquired institutional access, not inherited comprehension or a current cross-country proficient population.
learned_or_exposure_evidence: Schooling, media, migration and institutional history create acquired proficiency that changes by cohort/country.
shared_source_parallel_standard_reuse: Existing Russian resources are baseline overlap; parallel national-language editions may share formulas/semantic source but Russian is not an interlanguage to construct.
script_conversion_role: Cyrillic literacy cannot be transferred automatically to countries/communities shifting scripts.
speculative_construction: No.
math_worked_examples_modifier: Positive only for already proficient readers; no extra bridge bonus.
math_definition_theorem_modifier: No bonus beyond measured technical proficiency.
math_proof_modifier: No bonus beyond measured technical proficiency.
math_word_problem_modifier: No bonus beyond measured proficiency and context fit.
unique_gain_rule: Count only current Russian-proficient strata for whom a new Russian package adds access; often Russian instead reduces the marginal gain of another target as baseline overlap.
double_count_rule: Country×cohort×stage profiles; subtract national-language, English and other academic-language access; never use regional population.
uncertainty_and_evidence_gap: No harmonized current proficiency denominator; cohort and policy change; publication access source is chapter-level.
current_evidence_disposition: Existing overlap/control layer, not a constructed bridge recommendation.

code_status: stable learned code; no zero-study natural-language coverage
communities_potentially_served: Actual Esperanto learners/users who meet the educational endpoint
communities_explicitly_not_served: Any natural-language family or global population; readers inferred from European cognates; people not trained in Esperanto
scripts_or_modalities: Latin alphabet with Esperanto diacritics
zero_study_evidence: No zero-study natural-language coverage is established. The acquisition review concerns instructed Esperanto, not immediate comprehension.
learned_or_exposure_evidence: Maxwell's review says limited experiments support relative ease but are challengeable because many learning variables were uncontrolled; no technical-learning population or burden is established here.
shared_source_parallel_standard_reuse: A semantic source can generate an Esperanto edition for its learned community; it does not substitute for natural editions.
script_conversion_role: Unicode/diacritic handling is a rendering arm, not a major language bridge.
speculative_construction: No for the code; yes for global reach inferred from design.
evidence_grade: B-/C for learning; D for zero-study reach
math_worked_examples_modifier: Regular morphology may aid production after learning; no math-specific comprehension result.
math_definition_theorem_modifier: No credit absent proficiency.
math_proof_modifier: No credit absent proficiency.
math_word_problem_modifier: No credit absent proficiency.
unique_gain_rule: Count only actual proficient users lacking equivalent access, net of their other languages; include acquisition cost for any training-based intervention.
double_count_rule: No global/family multiplier; complete profile includes native languages, English/other L2s and Esperanto proficiency.
uncertainty_and_evidence_gap: Old heterogeneous acquisition experiments, no current census, no technical endpoint.
current_evidence_disposition: Learned-community target/control only.

code_status: contact practice, not universal standardized sign language
communities_potentially_served: Deaf signers with prior international contact or tested comprehension of a specified International Sign presentation; conference/expository endpoint only unless separately tested
communities_explicitly_not_served: All Deaf people; users of any national or village sign language by default; children needing a first/national sign language; non-signers
scripts_or_modalities: video/visual-gestural modality; captions, national sign-language versions and written text are separate modalities
zero_study_evidence: International Sign is a contact phenomenon; WFD guidance states it is not known by every deaf person. Empirical work is conference/expository and reports variation by sign source and signer experience; it is not zero-study universal comprehension.
learned_or_exposure_evidence: Acquired through international contact and adaptation. A study cited in the literature tested 32 Deaf participants in five countries; population reach and educational learning transfer remain unmeasured.
shared_source_parallel_standard_reuse: Can provide an additional international summary and reusable diagrams, but national/natural sign-language editions remain separate language products.
script_conversion_role: No script conversion: sign-language structure is independent of surrounding spoken/written languages; video production is a distinct modality cost.
speculative_construction: No for the contact practice; yes for treating it as a unified universal language or standardized replacement.
evidence_grade: B-/C for conference use; D for universal education
math_worked_examples_modifier: Spatial depiction may help diagrams for experienced users; this is not a universal math notation bridge.
math_definition_theorem_modifier: No automatic credit; technical lexicon, quantifiers and fingerspelling require language/contact proficiency.
math_proof_modifier: No automatic credit; referent tracking and discourse structure must be understood.
math_word_problem_modifier: No automatic credit; contextual language and numeracy signs vary.
unique_gain_rule: Count only tested signers crossing a specified expository/educational endpoint beyond their national sign, written and interpreted access.
double_count_rule: One signer once across national/village sign languages, International Sign experience, captions and written-language proficiency; never use global Deaf population.
uncertainty_and_evidence_gap: Sparse population-representative evidence, strong experience effects, no school-math endpoint, high modality/production heterogeneity.
current_evidence_disposition: Additional contact-layer summary only; never substitute for named sign-language editions.
